newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: COUNSELLOR SAYS GUILTY PLEA A SHOCK FOR MANY
The co-ordinator of counselling services for people affected by the Port Arthur shootings, says Martin Bryant's change of plea will still come as a shock for many.
In the Supreme Court in Hobart this morning, 29-year old Martin Bryant pleaded guilty to all charges brought against him in relation to the shootings.
In his previous court appearance on the 30th of September he pleaded not guilty.
Counsellor Rod McGregor told the ABC's World Today, people will still need to work through the accused's change of mind.
Mr McGregor says he thinks initial shock will be followed quite quickly by a sense of relief, then probably some intense grieving, before people can relax.
GROOM PREDICTS RELIEF IF PORT ARTHUR CASE OVER SOON
Tasmania's Attorney-General, Ray Groom says all Tasmanians must have a sense of great relief that the Martin Bryant case may soon be over.

In the Supreme Court in Hobart this morning, 29-year old Martin Bryant changed his plea to GUILTY in relation to all the charges brought against him following the Port Arthur shootings. Mr Groom says at least victims, their families and other witnesses will not have to go through the additional trauma of a full trial.
The Attorney-General has also praised the work of the Department of Public Prosecutions, other law officers and the police for their efforts in preparing the case for trial.
HOUSING UPTURN NEEDED-ECONOMIST
Access Economics director, Chris Richardson says yesterday's cut in official interest rates won't have any impact on the jobless rate until the housing industry picks up in the next six to 12 months.
The national jobless rate has risen point-one of a per cent to 8.8 percent.
Mr Richardson, has told ABC Radio that recovering sectors of the economy such as mining and farming are not ones which create substantial numbers of new jobs.
He says growth is needed to produce jobs, and that just won't happen until there's an upturn in the housing sector in the first half of next year.
SPOUSE MIGRATION LAWS LIKELY TO BE SLASHED
The Federal Government is likely to slash the number of people allowed to move to Australia under the spouse migration category as a response to the Senate disallowing new migration regulations.
Immigration Minister, Philip Ruddock, says the Senate's action this morning has prevented the Government from properly managing the migration program, by tightening certain categories.
Mr Ruddock says the Government will keep to its target of 74-thousand migrants next year, but it might now have to take fairly harsh measures to achieve the target.
A spokesman for Mr Ruddock says the Government might make a big cut in the largest category, spouse migration.
TABCORP TO COMPENSATE FOR COMPUTER CRASH
Victorian TAB agents who couldn't take bets during a central computer crash during Melbourne Cup day betting on Tuesday will be compensated by Tabcorp.
The Vice President of the TAB Agents Association, Evelyn Bakken, says some agents lost between 30 and 70 per cent of their expected takings.
The compensation is based on the amount an agent would have made during last Cup Day.
Ms Bakken says Tabcorp's decision has been welcomed by the agents involved who were paying staff double-time on Cup day.
KENTIALINK AIRLINE REMAINS GROUNDED
Kentialink Airlines remains grounded after presenting its case to Civil Aviation Authority to resume a service to Lord Howe Island.
The Airline lost its licence in October as part of the recommendations of the Seaview Air commission of Inquiry, set up after the fatal crash in 1994 of a Seaview plane.

Kenatialink's Managing Director, Ian Menzies says CASA has recognised the need for an air passenger service linking Lord Howe to the New South Wales far north coast, but is not convinced Kentialink should be the provider.
However Mr Menzies says he's confident Kentialink will be back in the air in the near future because the oustanding issue is not safety.
WILLIAM MILAT FINED $2000
The brother of convicted backpacker killer Ivan Milat has been fined A$2,000 for assaulting a photographer.
No conviction was recorded against 49-year-old William Milat who pleaded guilty to kicking and punching photographer Warren Clark and damaging his cameras.

His solicitor John Marsden told the Downing Centre Local court that his client's family had been subjected to the greatest invasion of privacy as a result of his brother being charged with the backpacker killings.
The magistrate agreed the assault took place under unusual circumstances saying it's appropriate there be no conviction, but he ordered Mr Milat pay a two-thousand-dollar fine. - - - -
CONCERNS OVER ARMY AVIATION UNIT
The Blackhawk inquiry has heard the SAS regiment was happier when the RAAF was conducting counter-terrorism operations, rather than the army's own aviation unit.
A military board of inquiry is trying to find the cause of a mid-air collision between two helicopters which killed 18 soldiers.
The commanding officer of the SAS Regiment Lieutenant Colonel Silverstone said while he was happy with the air force, he was unhappy with Five Aviation.
He said that was because it did not have the capacity to fly frequently enough to develop the capabilities required of it.
He said he was happy with the decision of the army to take over the Blackhawks but it was still learning how to manage its assets.
LABOR MP SAYS WOOLDRIDGE'S LOGIC "FLAWED"
The Federal Health Minister's been accused of using flawed logic in developing his plan to limit medicare provider numbers to graduating doctors.
Federal Labor MP, Allan Morris, says Minister Michael Wooldridge is yet to detail how the plan will save money.
Mr Morris says Doctor Wooldridge has set up a double standard, by retaining his own medicare provider number, but saying to about 400 doctors a year, that they can't have one.
Mr Morris says it's unreasonable for the Government to change the rules when some doctors have studied for eight years to go straight into general practice.
